extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: An open dataset of high-resolution Creative-Commons-licensed images sourced from Flickr and paired with synthetic BLIP-2 captions. CommonCatalog-C contains 26,232,417 images licensed for commercial use. CommonCatalog-NC contains 67,015,331 images, including CommonCatalog-C and additional images licensed for non-commercial use. Images with non-derivative licenses are excluded from training; their synthetic captions are released as an evaluation set.
extraction.license: Constituent images use CC-BY-2.0, CC-BY-SA-2.0, CC-BY-NC-2.0, or CC-BY-NC-SA-2.0 licenses. CommonCatalog-C includes the first two licenses; CommonCatalog-NC includes all four. Attribution is required. Non-derivative licenses are excluded from the training dataset.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan; A. Feder Cooper; Jasmine Collins; Landan Seguin; Austin Jacobson; Mihir Patel; Jonathan Frankle; Cory Stephenson; Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825v1 [cs.CV], 25 October 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors began with YFCC100M, which contains 100 million Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs. They re-scraped images from Flickr using IDs in the YFCC100M metadata to obtain high-resolution versions exceeding 4K. Images with non-derivative licenses were excluded from training. The remaining images were organized into commercial-use and non-commercial-use datasets, with the latter including the commercial-use subset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Almost all Creative-Commons images lack the captions needed for text-to-image training. CommonCatalog-C has alt text for 30.76% of images, and CommonCatalog-NC has alt text for 31.22%. Existing associated text often consists only of an image title or URL.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images downloaded directly from Flickr using Flickr IDs supplied in YFCC100M metadata. YFCC100M contains Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: The lack of usable captions was addressed through telephoning: a pretrained BLIP-2 model generated synthetic captions from images. The authors captioned all YFCC100M Creative-Commons images rather than relying on existing alt text.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For synthetic caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512 by 512 pixels. Images remained at their native resolution for diffusion-model training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images with non-derivative licenses were excluded from training. Remaining images were separated according to whether their licenses allowed commercial use. Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512 by 512 pixels before BLIP-2 captioning. For efficient diffusion-model training, image VAE latents and text-encoder embeddings were precomputed over the training dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic short-text captions were generated using pretrained BLIP-2 through the telephoning transfer-learning approach. The authors compared several captioning models and selected BLIP-2 based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. Captioning all YFCC100M Creative-Commons images required approximately 1,120 A100 GPU hours. Captions were also generated for excluded non-derivative images and released as an evaluation set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Qualitative comparison found that BLIP-2 captions were often more descriptive than LAION-2B alt-text captions, which could contain product names, irrelevant details, or poor grammar and syntax. The authors observed reduced n-gram diversity in synthetic captions, illustrated by a decrease in unique trigrams. The telephoning process is described as lossy compression that can omit identifying visual details.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pretrained BLIP-2; Section 4.2 identifies the model as BLIP-2 OPT2.5B, while Figure 5 labels it BLIP2-OPT-2.7B.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The image and synthetic-caption datasets are released on HuggingFace with associated data cards, with release information also available through the project GitHub URL. The authors plan to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources. No update schedule, versioning policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset provides an open-licensed alternative to web-scraped datasets with unclear image provenance and unresolved copyright questions. The authors argue that storing and distributing Creative-Commons images can avoid link rot and improve reproducibility. Models trained on the dataset are qualitatively less likely than SD2 to generate recognizable iconic characters, but adversarial prompts can still produce similar characters. The authors defer to legal experts on fair-use questions involving BLIP-2 and its pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The synthetic captions exhibit reduced n-gram diversity, including fewer unique trigrams. The source YFCC100M data is about a decade old, and its images are less current than those in LAION-2B.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only roughly 70 million usable Creative-Commons images were found, substantially fewer than the billions of images used by LAION-trained models. There are no ground-truth captions for the synthetic-caption training approach. Synthetic captioning loses information and reduces caption diversity. Models trained on CommonCatalog underperform in faces, general photography, and paintings. The source data is about a decade old, and the authors do not address its lack of currency.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image latent diffusion models, demonstrated through the CommonCanvas model family. Synthetic captions for excluded non-derivative images are released as an evaluation set. CommonCatalog-C supports commercial contexts; CommonCatalog-NC additionally includes images restricted to non-commercial contexts. Image use, adaptation, and remixing require attribution and compliance with the constituent licenses.
